Being able to factor integers in polynomial time in theory makes it practical to crack RSA encryption. RSA is public/private key encryption, which is the basis for essentially all of internet traffic. If you can break that, everything you can hoover up from the internet is viewable by you. But, "polynomial time" is still a potentially super expensive thing. If you have n things, and you can process them in n steps, that's polynomial time - linear. If you can process them in n^2 steps, that's also polynomial time, but it becomes super slow very quickly by the size of the input. n^1000 + n^800 + 10n^50 is also polynomial time, and that would be so ridiculous, it wouldn't make a difference. Assessment: Strongly bullish for 2027, conditional on approval and inflows
